# Paste-ready shell commands generated by a UI

When the page's output is a command the human copies into a terminal, the command *is*
the deliverable and its shape decides whether it works.

## Policy

- **The service renders the command and never executes it.** Deletes, moves and uploads
  stay in the human's hands; the UI says so in plain words ("nothing is deleted here").
  This matches the user's standing preference for reversible actions, so
  `gio trash` (or `trash-put`) must be a one-word swap from whatever the box generates.
- Prefer the reversible variant when the destructive one is not explicitly asked for, and
  mention the swap in the README rather than silently choosing.

## Shape

```bash
rm -- '/mnt/data2/ComfyUI/output/a file.png' \
     "/mnt/data2/ComfyUI/output/plain.png"   # WRONG: double quotes break on the apostrophe case
```

Rules that make a multi-line command paste cleanly:

1. **Absolute paths.** Pasting then works regardless of the cwd the terminal is in.
2. **Single quotes around every path**, with an inner single quote escaped as `'\''`
   (close quote, escaped literal, reopen). Verified against a name containing `it's`.
3. **Trailing backslash continuation, one path per line.** A multi-line paste into an
   interactive bash/zsh then runs as ONE command. With bare newlines the shell submits each
   line separately: the first line deletes and the remaining lines run as bogus commands.
4. **`--` end-of-options marker** right after the command (`rm -- `) so a path starting
   with `-` can never be read as a flag.
5. Build it in JS as a mapped join, e.g.
   `'rm -- ' + paths.map(p => "'" + p.replace(/'/g, "'\\''") + "'").join(' \\\n     ')`.
   Empty selection: hide the container and clear the value instead of showing a bare `rm --`.
6. Show the count and total size next to the box, and rebuild on every selection change —
   a stale command is worse than none.

## Verification (do not skip)

1. Harness the page (see SKILL.md) to produce the command from real page values.
2. Execute it verbatim in a scratch sandbox that contains the hostile names plus decoys,
   then diff the file list: only the selected entries may be gone.
3. Test one name per quoting class: plain, spaced, apostrophe, accented, dash-leading.
4. Only then run the same command on the real tree, and only if deletion is what the user
   actually asked for — the artifact's existence is the feature; running it is a separate
   decision.

## Clipboard

`navigator.clipboard` exists only in a secure context (https or localhost). On a plain
http:// LAN page it is `undefined`, so a Copy button that only calls it is dead in the
normal use case. Ship `document.execCommand('copy')` after `select()` as the fallback and
state it in the hint ("click the box and press Ctrl+C"). A harness that stubs only
`navigator.clipboard` certifies the branch the user never reaches.
